name: SOFIA
aliases: Study of Fesoterodine in an Aging Population
question: Does flexible-dose fesoterodine improve urgency compared with placebo in older adults with overactive bladder?

arms.label: Fesoterodine 4 mg daily with optional increase to 8 mg
matching placebo with sham dose adjustment

design.population: Adults aged 65 years or older with at least 3 months of overactive bladder symptoms, at least eight daily micturitions and three daily urgency episodes, moderate bladder bother, and MMSE score at least 20.
design.locator: PubMed abstract, Design, Setting, Participants, and Interventions

verdictNote: Urgency improved; urgency urinary incontinence did not differ significantly.
takeaway: In adults aged 65 or older with overactive bladder, flexible-dose fesoterodine 4 or 8 mg reduced urgency episodes more than placebo at 12 weeks; urgency urinary incontinence episodes did not differ significantly.

reports.label: 12-week randomized report
reports.citation: Wagg A, Khullar V, Marschall-Kehrel D, et al. "Flexible-Dose Fesoterodine in Elderly Adults with Overactive Bladder: Results of the Randomized, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled Study of Fesoterodine in an Aging Population Trial." *J Am Geriatr Soc.* 2013;61(2):185-193. doi:10.1111/jgs.12088

results.measure: Change from baseline in episodes per 24 hours at week 12
results.note: The abstract reports a statistically significant between-group difference without arm-specific changes or an effect estimate.
The abstract reports no statistically significant between-group difference and gives no arm-specific changes.
The abstract reports no change in MMSE score, without group-specific values.

harms.label: Dry mouth
harms.note: The abstract does not give event counts or arm-specific safety denominators.

harms.label: Constipation
harms.note: The abstract does not give event counts or arm-specific safety denominators.

delivery.label: Dose adjustment
delivery.value: Fesoterodine began at 4 mg; increase to 8 mg was allowed at week 4 or 8, with de-escalation to 4 mg at week 8; placebo adjustments were sham.

delivery.label: Dose escalation choice by week 8
delivery.note: The placebo group made a sham escalation choice; the abstract does not give counts or denominators.

reports.dateLocator: Crossref record, published-online; PubMed citation, Epub

reports.label: 12-week open-label extension
reports.citation: Wagg A, Khullar V, Michel MC, et al. "Long-term safety, tolerability and efficacy of flexible-dose fesoterodine in elderly patients with overactive bladder: Open-label extension of the SOFIA trial." *Neurourol Urodyn.* 2014;33(1):106-114. doi:10.1002/nau.22383

results.measure: Bladder-diary and patient-reported outcomes at end of open-label extension
results.note: The prior-fesoterodine group maintained its response; the prior-placebo group improved after starting fesoterodine. No arm-specific efficacy values appear in the abstract.

harms.label: Any adverse event during open-label fesoterodine
harms.note: Groups are defined by original randomized assignment; both received fesoterodine during the extension. Arm-specific denominators are absent from the abstract.

harms.label: Discontinued because of an adverse event during extension
harms.note: Groups are defined by original randomized assignment; both received fesoterodine during the extension. Arm-specific denominators are absent from the abstract.

delivery.label: Open-label entrants and treatment
delivery.value: 654 prior trial completers entered; prior-placebo patients began fesoterodine 4 mg with optional increase to 8 mg, and prior-fesoterodine patients continued their assigned dose.
